record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: For the clamped plate eigenvalues Γ₁ ≤ Γ₂ ≤ ··· and the buckling eigenvalues Λ₁ ≤ Λ₂ ≤ ··· on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, is the ball the maximizer of the first nontrivial ratios Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁? More generally, what are the sharp upper bounds for ratios such as Γ_{m+1}/Γ_m, Λ_{m+1}/Λ_m, (Γ₂+Γ₃)/Γ₁, and (Λ₂+Λ₃)/Λ₁?

evidence.quote: One could also investigate combinations of eigenvalues of the clamped plate and buckling problems ... one should begin with the ratios Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁ ... but the natural conjectures that Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁ should be maximized when Ω is an n-ball are as yet unproved.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with sufficiently smooth boundary. Consider two fourth-order eigenvalue problems on $\Omega$:

(a) The clamped plate problem
$$\Delta^2 u = \Gamma\, u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
with eigenvalues $0 < \Gamma_1 \le \Gamma_2 \le \Gamma_3 \le \cdots$.

(b) The buckling problem
$$\Delta^2 u = -\Lambda\, \Delta u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
with eigenvalues $0 < \Lambda_1 \le \Lambda_2 \le \Lambda_3 \le \cdots$.

Among all bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (with fixed volume, say), determine:

1. Whether the ball maximizes the first nontrivial ratios $\Gamma_2/\Gamma_1$ and $\Lambda_2/\Lambda_1$, i.e. prove or disprove that
$$\frac{\Gamma_2(\Omega)}{\Gamma_1(\Omega)} \le \frac{\Gamma_2(B)}{\Gamma_1(B)}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_2(\Omega)}{\Lambda_1(\Omega)} \le \frac{\Lambda_2(B)}{\Lambda_1(B)},$$
where $B$ is a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

2. More generally, find sharp upper bounds (and identify the extremal domains) for the ratios
$$\frac{\Gamma_{m+1}}{\Gamma_m}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_{m+1}}{\Lambda_m}, \qquad \frac{\Gamma_2 + \Gamma_3}{\Gamma_1}, \qquad \frac{\Lambda_2 + \Lambda_3}{\Lambda_1}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The underlying Rayleigh conjecture for the first clamped-plate eigenvalue is known only in dimensions 2 (Nadirashvili) and 3 (Ashbaugh–Benguria), and the Pólya–Szegő conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue remains open in general. The corresponding sharp upper bounds for the ratios Γ_{m+1}/Γ_m, Λ_{m+1}/Λ_m, (Γ_2+Γ_3)/Γ_1, (Λ_2+Λ_3)/Λ_1, and even the ball-maximizer conjectures for Γ_2/Γ_1 and Λ_2/Λ_1, do not appear to be established in the recent literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards the optimality of the ball for the Rayleigh Conjecture concerning the clamped plate
status_evidence.snippet: Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate proven in 2D (Nadirashvili) and 3D (Ashbaugh-Benguria); remains open in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational first-eigenvalue conjectures are still open in higher dimensions, indicating ratio conjectures remain unproved.

status_evidence.title: Minimization of the buckling load of a clamped plate with perimeter constraint
status_evidence.snippet: The Pólya–Szegő conjecture on the first buckling eigenvalue remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The buckling first-eigenvalue ball conjecture remains open, so the higher-ratio analogues are unsettled.
